reason: The cited evidence describes tribo-oxidation forming a nanocrystalline oxide glaze on Ni-based HEAs containing Al, Nb, etc., and notes its anti-wear properties, but it does not demonstrate a pre-service heat treatment to induce the glaze, nor does it provide friction or wear rate data supporting the specific predicted improvements or the full temperature range claimed.
premises: Al in Ni-based HEA can be preferentially oxidized by heat treatment to form an oxide layer
The resulting oxide layer is nanocrystalline and acts as a lubricious glaze
The oxide glaze is self-healing and regenerates during cyclic sliding wear
The glaze reduces friction (to ~0.15) and wear (by >1 order of magnitude) vs. untreated alloy
The effect persists from room temperature to 800 °C under controlled oxidation
